"""Independent real-model revision and fitting-full-source experiments."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import shutil
import time
from contextlib import ExitStack, contextmanager
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

from tests.manual import research_branch_review as branch
from tests.manual import research_framework_comparison as framework
from tests.manual import research_guidance_simplification_ab as shared


def revision_args(session, store, args, *, reject_noop=False):
    """Expand explicit changed fields from an actually read immutable version."""
    rows = []
    for change in args["changes"]:
        if set(change) != {"value"} or not isinstance(change["value"], dict):
            raise ValueError("Each change needs value with id and changed fields; the program supplies the read version.")
        patch_value = change["value"]
        identity = patch_value.get("id")
        if not isinstance(identity, str) or not identity:
            raise ValueError("An exact knowledge id is required.")
        read = None
        for result in reversed(list(session._memory_results.values())):
            if not result.ok or result.call.name != "knowledge_read" or result.call.args.get("id") != identity:
                continue
            try:
                value = json.loads(result.model_text)
            except (ValueError, TypeError):
                continue
            if isinstance(value, dict) and value.get("id") == identity and type(value.get("revision")) is int:
                read = store.repository.read(identity, value["revision"])
                break
        if read is None:
            # Existing identities require a read, never a silent refresh to HEAD.
            if store.repository.read(identity) is not None:
                raise ValueError("Read this exact stored object with knowledge_read before changing it.")
            complete = patch_value
            expected = 0
        else:
            complete = {**read.value.to_dict(), **patch_value}
            expected = read.revision
            if reject_noop and complete == read.value.to_dict():
                raise ValueError("No fields differ from the version you read; no changes written. "
                                 "Do not resubmit unchanged edits. Continue the answer using original evidence, "
                                 "or read again if you intend a different update.")
        rows.append({"value": complete, "expected_revision": expected})
    return {**args, "changes": rows}


def revision_spec(spec):
    from codey.research.knowledge_schema import mutation_schema
    from codey.toolchain.tool_spec import freeze_spec_parameters, thaw_schema_value

    params = thaw_schema_value(dict(spec.parameters))
    # The experiment retains its original full-value control even after the
    # current production tool has adopted flat partial edits.
    params["changes"]["items"] = mutation_schema()
    params["changes"]["items"]["properties"]["value"]["properties"]["kind"]["enum"] = [
        "claim", "inference", "question", "entity", "observation"]
    row = params["changes"]["items"]
    row["properties"].pop("expected_revision")
    row["required"] = ["value"]
    row["properties"]["value"]["required"] = ["id"]
    example = {"tool": "knowledge_commit", "args": {"commit_id": "retitle-1", "changes": [
        {"value": {"id": "exact-id-from-knowledge-read", "title": "Updated title"}}]}}
    description = (
        "Change stored knowledge: first knowledge_read the exact id, then send value containing that id and only "
        "the fields to change. The application preserves omitted fields and uses the version actually read; "
        "do not send expected_revision or revision. Existing id means update, not a replacement object. "
        "For a new object, provide id, kind, content and origin. Only claim/inference/question/entity/observation "
        "are allowed. Use exact database references, never eN labels. Reuse commit_id only for an identical retry."
    )
    return freeze_spec_parameters(replace(spec, parameters=tuple(params.items()), description=description,
                                          json_examples=(json.dumps(example),)))


def flat_revision_args(session, store, args, *, reject_noop=False):
    return revision_args(session, store, {**args, "changes": [{"value": row} for row in args["changes"]]},
                         reject_noop=reject_noop)


def flat_revision_spec(spec):
    from codey.toolchain.tool_spec import freeze_spec_parameters, thaw_schema_value

    result = revision_spec(spec)
    params = thaw_schema_value(dict(result.parameters))
    params["changes"]["items"] = params["changes"]["items"]["properties"]["value"]
    params["changes"]["minItems"] = 1
    description = (
        "Edit an existing object after knowledge_read: changes contains its exact id and only fields to change. "
        "The program preserves other fields and checks the version actually read. Example: "
        '{"commit_id":"retitle-1","changes":[{"id":"exact-read-id","title":"New title"}]}. '
        "Do not wrap each change in value. Do not supply revision or expected_revision. "
        "A successful commit is already saved; do not submit it again with a new commit_id or create a replacement "
        "through knowledge_updates. For an explicitly requested new object, include id, kind, content and origin. "
        "Only claim/inference/question/entity/observation are allowed; references use exact database ids and versions."
    )
    return freeze_spec_parameters(replace(result, parameters=tuple(params.items()), description=description,
                                          json_examples=()))


def committed_view(original, session, ledger, scope, visible, *, include_changes=False):
    from codey.knowledge.model import canonical_json

    text = original(session, ledger, scope, visible)
    text = text.split("\n\nKnowledge changes already committed (not evidence; do not repeat):\n", 1)[0]
    commits = [{**json.loads(result.model_text), **({"changes": result.call.args["changes"]} if include_changes else {})}
               for result in session._memory_results.values() if result.ok and result.call.name == "knowledge_commit"]
    if commits:
        text += "\n\nKnowledge changes already committed (not evidence; do not repeat):\n" + canonical_json(commits)
    return text


def expanded_read(delegate, call, opened, provider):
    """Offer the remaining HTML only when every current original still fits."""
    from codey.research.answer_context import _render_context
    from codey.research.answer_contract import AnswerScope, answer_scope
    from codey.research.passages import describe_document_window, render_passage_window, restore_passages
    from codey.research.source_document import SourceDocument
    from codey.research.source_rendering import render_opened_source
    from codey.utils.text_budget import estimate_tokens

    if (not opened.ok or not isinstance(delegate._research_scope, AnswerScope)
            or "limit" in call.args or call.args.get("pages") or not opened.read_passages):
        return opened
    observation = opened.read_observation
    source = observation.get("source", {})
    text = observation.get("text", "")
    if source.get("content_kind") != "html" or opened.read_passages[-1]["end"] >= len(text):
        return opened
    document = SourceDocument.html(requested_url=source["requested_url"], final_url=source["final_url"],
                                   title=source["title"], text=text, truncated=source["truncated"])
    rows = describe_document_window(document, source["text_hash"], opened.read_passages[0]["start"],
                                    len(text), coherent=True)
    session = delegate.session.clone_projection()
    ledger = delegate.research_tools.ledger.clone()
    restore_passages(ledger, observation, rows)
    from codey.runtime.core.models import ToolResult

    session._memory_results["proposed_full_read"] = ToolResult(
        call=call, model_text="", ok=True, canonical={"read_passages": rows})
    scope = answer_scope(session)
    view = _render_context(session, ledger, scope, scope.aliases)
    budget = getattr(provider, "context_budget", None)
    counter = getattr(provider, "count_text", None)
    cap = min(budget.window_tokens // 2, budget.input_limit) if budget else 16384
    try:
        count = counter(view, deadline=time.monotonic() + 30).value if callable(counter) else estimate_tokens(view)
    except (ValueError, TimeoutError, OSError):
        return opened
    if type(count) is not int or not 0 <= count <= cap:
        return opened
    body = render_opened_source(document, render_passage_window(document, rows),
                                read_window=(rows[0]["start"], rows[-1]["end"]))
    return replace(opened, model_text=body, read_passages=tuple(rows))


@contextmanager
def treatment(arm):
    from codey.operations import provider_session
    from codey.operations.task_execution import ExecutionDelegate
    from codey.research import answer_contract

    with ExitStack() as stack:
        if arm in {"revision", "revision_flat", "revision_flat_noop", "revision_visible"}:
            old_spec = answer_contract.answer_spec
            old_commit = ExecutionDelegate._commit_research_knowledge

            def spec(value, scope):
                result = old_spec(value, scope)
                transform = revision_spec if arm == "revision" else flat_revision_spec
                return transform(result) if result.name == "knowledge_commit" else result

            def commit(self, call, tools):
                from codey.research.answer_contract import AnswerScope

                if not isinstance(self._research_scope, AnswerScope):
                    return old_commit(self, call, tools)
                normalize = revision_args if arm == "revision" else flat_revision_args
                args = normalize(self.session, tools.store, call.args,
                                 reject_noop=arm in {"revision_flat_noop", "revision_visible"})
                from codey.runtime.core.models import ToolResult

                if any(row["value"].get("kind") not in {"claim", "inference", "question", "entity", "observation"}
                       for row in args["changes"]):
                    raise ValueError("whole research knowledge_commit only accumulates explicit claims, inferences, "
                                     "questions, entities or observations; answer publication owns source/evidence/answer")
                outcome = tools.knowledge_commit(args)
                return ToolResult(call=call, model_text=outcome.model_text, ok=outcome.ok), outcome.ok, None

            stack.enter_context(patch.object(answer_contract, "answer_spec", spec))
            stack.enter_context(patch.object(ExecutionDelegate, "_commit_research_knowledge", commit))
            if arm in {"revision_flat", "revision_flat_noop", "revision_visible"}:
                from codey.research import answer_context

                original_view = answer_context._render_context

                def view(*args):
                    return committed_view(original_view, *args, include_changes=arm == "revision_visible")

                stack.enter_context(patch.object(answer_context, "_render_context", view))
        if arm == "full_read":
            provider = None
            old_provider = provider_session.ObservedProvider
            old_opened = ExecutionDelegate._opened_result

            def observed(*args, **kwargs):
                nonlocal provider
                provider = old_provider(*args, **kwargs)
                return provider

            def opened(self, call, output, url, **kwargs):
                output = expanded_read(self, call, output, provider)
                return old_opened(self, call, output, url, **kwargs)

            stack.enter_context(patch.object(provider_session, "ObservedProvider", observed))
            stack.enter_context(patch.object(ExecutionDelegate, "_opened_result", opened))
        yield


def worker(root, directory, base_url, case, seed, arm):
    with patch.object(branch, "ablation", treatment):
        branch.worker(root, directory, base_url, case, seed, arm)


def prepare(root):
    previous = Path(".e2e-artifacts/research-direct-tools-prior-knowledge-20261103")
    long_root = Path(".e2e-artifacts/research-guidance-production-20261104")
    root.mkdir(exist_ok=False)
    for name in ("clock-context.txt", "material-channel.json", "seed-identities.json"):
        shutil.copy2(previous / name, root / name)
    for name in ("warm-knowledge", "empty-knowledge", "revision-knowledge", "conflict-knowledge"):
        shutil.copytree(previous / name, root / name)
    old = {r["id"]: r for r in framework.read_json(previous / "fixtures.json")["cases"]}
    long = {r["id"]: r for r in framework.read_json(long_root / "fixtures.json")["cases"]}
    revision = {**old["revise"], "id": "revise_alias", "question": old["revise"]["question"].replace(
        "把它的标题改为‘只读 WAL 条件（核查修订）’，只改变标题", "为它追加别名‘已核查只读条件’，只改变 aliases，保留已有别名")}
    synthetic = {**long["synthetic_conditions"], "id": "long_synthetic"}
    doc = dict(synthetic["documents"][0])
    paragraphs = doc["text"].splitlines()
    filler = "This section catalogues archive labels; it adds no policy conditions or performance measurements. " * 55
    doc["text"] = ("\n".join(paragraphs[:2]) + "\n\n## Archive background\n\n" + filler
                   + "\n\n" + "\n".join(paragraphs[2:-2]) + "\n\n## Archive background continued\n\n"
                   + filler + "\n\n" + "\n".join(paragraphs[-2:]))
    synthetic["documents"] = [doc]
    cases = [old["revise"], revision, long["long"], synthetic, old["history"], old["accumulate"]]
    framework.write_json(root / "fixtures.json", {"schema_version": 1, "cases": cases})
    framework.write_json(root / "limits.json", {"turns": 18, "requests": 12, "process_seconds": 900, "agent_seconds": 840})
    framework.write_json(root / "preregistration.json", {
        "phase": "A/B", "seeds": [703, 704],
        "matrix": [{"case": r["id"], "arms": ["baseline", "revision_flat" if r["id"].startswith("revise")
                    or r["id"] in {"history", "accumulate"} else "full_read"]} for r in cases],
        "gate": "Target correctness first; database revision and preserved metadata separately checked. No new semantic regression.",
        "limitations": "Two seeds, fixed sources; full-read candidate applies only to default HTML reads fitting the whole work-view budget.",
    })


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("action", choices=("prepare", "freeze", "run", "worker"))
    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--directory", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--base-url")
    parser.add_argument("--case")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--arm")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    root = args.root.resolve()
    if args.action == "prepare":
        prepare(root)
    elif args.action == "freeze":
        shared.freeze(root)
        hashes = framework.read_json(root / "frozen-inputs.json")
        for folder in ("revision-knowledge", "conflict-knowledge", "baseline-code"):
            for path in (root / folder).rglob("*"):
                if path.is_file():
                    hashes[path.relative_to(root).as_posix()] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        framework.write_json(root / "frozen-inputs.json", hashes)
        branch.verify(root)
        print("FROZEN", root, flush=True)
    elif args.action == "worker":
        worker(root, args.directory, args.base_url, args.case, args.seed, args.arm)
    else:
        spec = framework.read_json(root / "preregistration.json")
        rows = framework.read_json(root / "matrix.json") if (root / "matrix.json").exists() else []
        with patch.object(shared, "__spec__", SimpleNamespace(name=__spec__.name)):
            for index, item in enumerate(spec["matrix"]):
                if args.case and args.case != item["case"]:
                    continue
                for seed in spec["seeds"]:
                    if args.seed is not None and seed != args.seed:
                        continue
                    arms = item["arms"]
                    shift = (seed + index) % len(arms)
                    for arm in arms[shift:] + arms[:shift]:
                        if args.arm and arm != args.arm:
                            continue
                        if any((r["case"], r["seed"], r["arm"]) == (item["case"], seed, arm) for r in rows):
                            continue
                        print("START", item["case"], seed, arm, flush=True)
                        row = shared.run_one(root, item["case"], seed, arm)
                        rows.append(row)
                        framework.write_json(root / "matrix.json", rows)
                        print("END", item["case"], seed, arm, row.get("result"), flush=True)
                        framework.backend_ready()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

### SQLite 只读打开 WAL 数据库的分析

**1. 支持的版本**
SQLite 从 **3.22.0 (2018-01-22)** 版本开始支持在只读媒体或缺乏写权限的情况下读取 WAL 模式数据库 [e1]。

**2. 替代条件**
在较新版本的 SQLite 中，即使数据库处于只读媒体或缺乏写权限，只要满足以下条件之一，仍可以读取 WAL 模式数据库 [e1]：
*   `-shm` 和 `-wal` 文件已经存在且可读。
*   包含数据库的目录具有写权限，以便可以创建 `-shm` 和 `-wal` 文件。
*   数据库连接是使用 `immutable` 查询参数打开的。

**最佳实践提示：**
虽然可以打开只读的 WAL 模式数据库，但将数据库转换为 `PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE` 后再烧录到只读媒体上是一个良好的实践 [e1]。

## 引用来源
[e1] SQLite WAL read-only databases (frozen official excerpt) — https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html (source 5fa34fc8ef85871a, 0:915)

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 5. Read-Only Databases

Older versions of SQLite could not read a WAL-mode database that was
read-only. In other words, write access was required in order to read a
WAL-mode database. This constraint was relaxed beginning with
SQLite version 3.22.0 (2018-01-22).

On newer versions of SQLite,
a WAL-mode database on read-only media, or a WAL-mode database that lacks
write permission, can still be read as long as one or more of the following
conditions are met:

The -shm and -wal files already exist and are readable.

There is write permission on the directory containing the database so
that the -shm and -wal files can be created.

The database connection is opened using the
immutable query parameter.

Even though it is possible to open a read-only WAL-mode database,
it is good practice to convert the database to PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE prior to burning an
SQLite database image onto read-only media.

"""Independent real-model revision and fitting-full-source experiments."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import shutil
import time
from contextlib import ExitStack, contextmanager
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

from tests.manual import research_branch_review as branch
from tests.manual import research_framework_comparison as framework
from tests.manual import research_guidance_simplification_ab as shared


def revision_args(session, store, args, *, reject_noop=False):
    """Expand explicit changed fields from an actually read immutable version."""
    rows = []
    for change in args["changes"]:
        if set(change) != {"value"} or not isinstance(change["value"], dict):
            raise ValueError("Each change needs value with id and changed fields; the program supplies the read version.")
        patch_value = change["value"]
        identity = patch_value.get("id")
        if not isinstance(identity, str) or not identity:
            raise ValueError("An exact knowledge id is required.")
        read = None
        for result in reversed(list(session._memory_results.values())):
            if not result.ok or result.call.name != "knowledge_read" or result.call.args.get("id") != identity:
                continue
            try:
                value = json.loads(result.model_text)
            except (ValueError, TypeError):
                continue
            if isinstance(value, dict) and value.get("id") == identity and type(value.get("revision")) is int:
                read = store.repository.read(identity, value["revision"])
                break
        if read is None:
            # Existing identities require a read, never a silent refresh to HEAD.
            if store.repository.read(identity) is not None:
                raise ValueError("Read this exact stored object with knowledge_read before changing it.")
            complete = patch_value
            expected = 0
        else:
            complete = {**read.value.to_dict(), **patch_value}
            expected = read.revision
            if reject_noop and complete == read.value.to_dict():
                raise ValueError("No fields differ from the version you read; no changes written. "
                                 "Do not resubmit unchanged edits. Continue the answer using original evidence, "
                                 "or read again if you intend a different update.")
        rows.append({"value": complete, "expected_revision": expected})
    return {**args, "changes": rows}


def revision_spec(spec):
    from codey.research.knowledge_schema import mutation_schema
    from codey.toolchain.tool_spec import freeze_spec_parameters, thaw_schema_value

    params = thaw_schema_value(dict(spec.parameters))
    # The experiment retains its original full-value control even after the
    # current production tool has adopted flat partial edits.
    params["changes"]["items"] = mutation_schema()
    params["changes"]["items"]["properties"]["value"]["properties"]["kind"]["enum"] = [
        "claim", "inference", "question", "entity", "observation"]
    row = params["changes"]["items"]
    row["properties"].pop("expected_revision")
    row["required"] = ["value"]
    row["properties"]["value"]["required"] = ["id"]
    example = {"tool": "knowledge_commit", "args": {"commit_id": "retitle-1", "changes": [
        {"value": {"id": "exact-id-from-knowledge-read", "title": "Updated title"}}]}}
    description = (
        "Change stored knowledge: first knowledge_read the exact id, then send value containing that id and only "
        "the fields to change. The application preserves omitted fields and uses the version actually read; "
        "do not send expected_revision or revision. Existing id means update, not a replacement object. "
        "For a new object, provide id, kind, content and origin. Only claim/inference/question/entity/observation "
        "are allowed. Use exact database references, never eN labels. Reuse commit_id only for an identical retry."
    )
    return freeze_spec_parameters(replace(spec, parameters=tuple(params.items()), description=description,
                                          json_examples=(json.dumps(example),)))


def flat_revision_args(session, store, args, *, reject_noop=False):
    return revision_args(session, store, {**args, "changes": [{"value": row} for row in args["changes"]]},
                         reject_noop=reject_noop)


def flat_revision_spec(spec):
    from codey.toolchain.tool_spec import freeze_spec_parameters, thaw_schema_value

    result = revision_spec(spec)
    params = thaw_schema_value(dict(result.parameters))
    params["changes"]["items"] = params["changes"]["items"]["properties"]["value"]
    params["changes"]["minItems"] = 1
    description = (
        "Edit an existing object after knowledge_read: changes contains its exact id and only fields to change. "
        "The program preserves other fields and checks the version actually read. Example: "
        '{"commit_id":"retitle-1","changes":[{"id":"exact-read-id","title":"New title"}]}. '
        "Do not wrap each change in value. Do not supply revision or expected_revision. "
        "A successful commit is already saved; do not submit it again with a new commit_id or create a replacement "
        "through knowledge_updates. For an explicitly requested new object, include id, kind, content and origin. "
        "Only claim/inference/question/entity/observation are allowed; references use exact database ids and versions."
    )
    return freeze_spec_parameters(replace(result, parameters=tuple(params.items()), description=description,
                                          json_examples=()))


def explicit_creation_args(session, store, args):
    """A misspelled edit identity must never implicitly create a new object."""
    rows = []
    for fields in args["changes"]:
        fields = dict(fields)
        create = fields.pop("create", False)
        if create is True:
            rows.append({"value": fields, "expected_revision": 0})
        else:
            identity = fields.get("id")
            if not isinstance(identity, str) or store.repository.read(identity) is None:
                raise ValueError("Unknown edit id. Copy the exact id from knowledge_read; an edit cannot create a replacement.")
            rows.extend(flat_revision_args(session, store, {**args, "changes": [fields]}, reject_noop=True)["changes"])
    return {**args, "changes": rows}


def explicit_creation_spec(spec):
    from codey.toolchain.tool_spec import freeze_spec_parameters, thaw_schema_value

    result = flat_revision_spec(spec)
    params = thaw_schema_value(dict(result.parameters))
    params["changes"]["items"]["properties"]["create"] = {"type": "boolean", "const": True,
        "description": "Only for an explicitly requested new object; never a fallback for an edit error."}
    description = result.description.replace(
        "For an explicitly requested new object, include id, kind, content and origin.",
        "An edit id must already exist and have been read. Only for an explicitly requested NEW object, "
        "set create=true and include id, kind, content and origin. Never use create=true to work around an edit error.")
    return freeze_spec_parameters(replace(result, parameters=tuple(params.items()), description=description))


def committed_view(original, session, ledger, scope, visible, *, include_changes=False):
    from codey.knowledge.model import canonical_json

    text = original(session, ledger, scope, visible)
    text = text.split("\n\nKnowledge changes already committed (not evidence; do not repeat):\n", 1)[0]
    commits = [{**json.loads(result.model_text), **({"changes": result.call.args["changes"]} if include_changes else {})}
               for result in session._memory_results.values() if result.ok and result.call.name == "knowledge_commit"]
    if commits:
        text += "\n\nKnowledge changes already committed (not evidence; do not repeat):\n" + canonical_json(commits)
    return text


def expanded_read(delegate, call, opened, provider):
    """Offer the remaining HTML only when every current original still fits."""
    from codey.research.answer_context import _render_context
    from codey.research.answer_contract import AnswerScope, answer_scope
    from codey.research.passages import describe_document_window, render_passage_window, restore_passages
    from codey.research.source_document import SourceDocument
    from codey.research.source_rendering import render_opened_source
    from codey.utils.text_budget import estimate_tokens

    if (not opened.ok or not isinstance(delegate._research_scope, AnswerScope)
            or "limit" in call.args or call.args.get("pages") or not opened.read_passages):
        return opened
    observation = opened.read_observation
    source = observation.get("source", {})
    text = observation.get("text", "")
    if source.get("content_kind") != "html" or opened.read_passages[-1]["end"] >= len(text):
        return opened
    document = SourceDocument.html(requested_url=source["requested_url"], final_url=source["final_url"],
                                   title=source["title"], text=text, truncated=source["truncated"])
    rows = describe_document_window(document, source["text_hash"], opened.read_passages[0]["start"],
                                    len(text), coherent=True)
    session = delegate.session.clone_projection()
    ledger = delegate.research_tools.ledger.clone()
    restore_passages(ledger, observation, rows)
    from codey.runtime.core.models import ToolResult

    session._memory_results["proposed_full_read"] = ToolResult(
        call=call, model_text="", ok=True, canonical={"read_passages": rows})
    scope = answer_scope(session)
    view = _render_context(session, ledger, scope, scope.aliases)
    budget = getattr(provider, "context_budget", None)
    counter = getattr(provider, "count_text", None)
    cap = min(budget.window_tokens // 2, budget.input_limit) if budget else 16384
    try:
        count = counter(view, deadline=time.monotonic() + 30).value if callable(counter) else estimate_tokens(view)
    except (ValueError, TimeoutError, OSError):
        return opened
    if type(count) is not int or not 0 <= count <= cap:
        return opened
    body = render_opened_source(document, render_passage_window(document, rows),
                                read_window=(rows[0]["start"], rows[-1]["end"]))
    return replace(opened, model_text=body, read_passages=tuple(rows))


@contextmanager
def treatment(arm):
    from codey.operations import provider_session
    from codey.operations.task_execution import ExecutionDelegate
    from codey.research import answer_contract

    with ExitStack() as stack:
        if arm in {"revision", "revision_flat", "revision_flat_noop", "revision_visible", "revision_explicit_create"}:
            old_spec = answer_contract.answer_spec
            old_commit = ExecutionDelegate._commit_research_knowledge

            def spec(value, scope):
                result = old_spec(value, scope)
                transform = (revision_spec if arm == "revision" else
                             explicit_creation_spec if arm == "revision_explicit_create" else flat_revision_spec)
                return transform(result) if result.name == "knowledge_commit" else result

            def commit(self, call, tools):
                from codey.research.answer_contract import AnswerScope

                if not isinstance(self._research_scope, AnswerScope):
                    return old_commit(self, call, tools)
                normalize = revision_args if arm == "revision" else flat_revision_args
                args = (explicit_creation_args(self.session, tools.store, call.args) if arm == "revision_explicit_create"
                        else normalize(self.session, tools.store, call.args,
                                       reject_noop=arm in {"revision_flat_noop", "revision_visible"}))
                from codey.runtime.core.models import ToolResult

                if any(row["value"].get("kind") not in {"claim", "inference", "question", "entity", "observation"}
                       for row in args["changes"]):
                    raise ValueError("whole research knowledge_commit only accumulates explicit claims, inferences, "
                                     "questions, entities or observations; answer publication owns source/evidence/answer")
                outcome = tools.knowledge_commit(args)
                return ToolResult(call=call, model_text=outcome.model_text, ok=outcome.ok), outcome.ok, None

            stack.enter_context(patch.object(answer_contract, "answer_spec", spec))
            stack.enter_context(patch.object(ExecutionDelegate, "_commit_research_knowledge", commit))
            if arm in {"revision_flat", "revision_flat_noop", "revision_visible", "revision_explicit_create"}:
                from codey.research import answer_context

                original_view = answer_context._render_context

                def view(*args):
                    return committed_view(original_view, *args, include_changes=arm == "revision_visible")

                stack.enter_context(patch.object(answer_context, "_render_context", view))
        if arm == "full_read":
            provider = None
            old_provider = provider_session.ObservedProvider
            old_opened = ExecutionDelegate._opened_result

            def observed(*args, **kwargs):
                nonlocal provider
                provider = old_provider(*args, **kwargs)
                return provider

            def opened(self, call, output, url, **kwargs):
                output = expanded_read(self, call, output, provider)
                return old_opened(self, call, output, url, **kwargs)

            stack.enter_context(patch.object(provider_session, "ObservedProvider", observed))
            stack.enter_context(patch.object(ExecutionDelegate, "_opened_result", opened))
        yield


def worker(root, directory, base_url, case, seed, arm):
    with patch.object(branch, "ablation", treatment):
        branch.worker(root, directory, base_url, case, seed, arm)


def prepare(root):
    previous = Path(".e2e-artifacts/research-direct-tools-prior-knowledge-20261103")
    long_root = Path(".e2e-artifacts/research-guidance-production-20261104")
    root.mkdir(exist_ok=False)
    for name in ("clock-context.txt", "material-channel.json", "seed-identities.json"):
        shutil.copy2(previous / name, root / name)
    for name in ("warm-knowledge", "empty-knowledge", "revision-knowledge", "conflict-knowledge"):
        shutil.copytree(previous / name, root / name)
    old = {r["id"]: r for r in framework.read_json(previous / "fixtures.json")["cases"]}
    long = {r["id"]: r for r in framework.read_json(long_root / "fixtures.json")["cases"]}
    revision = {**old["revise"], "id": "revise_alias", "question": old["revise"]["question"].replace(
        "把它的标题改为‘只读 WAL 条件（核查修订）’，只改变标题", "为它追加别名‘已核查只读条件’，只改变 aliases，保留已有别名")}
    synthetic = {**long["synthetic_conditions"], "id": "long_synthetic"}
    doc = dict(synthetic["documents"][0])
    paragraphs = doc["text"].splitlines()
    filler = "This section catalogues archive labels; it adds no policy conditions or performance measurements. " * 55
    doc["text"] = ("\n".join(paragraphs[:2]) + "\n\n## Archive background\n\n" + filler
                   + "\n\n" + "\n".join(paragraphs[2:-2]) + "\n\n## Archive background continued\n\n"
                   + filler + "\n\n" + "\n".join(paragraphs[-2:]))
    synthetic["documents"] = [doc]
    cases = [old["revise"], revision, long["long"], synthetic, old["history"], old["accumulate"]]
    framework.write_json(root / "fixtures.json", {"schema_version": 1, "cases": cases})
    framework.write_json(root / "limits.json", {"turns": 18, "requests": 12, "process_seconds": 900, "agent_seconds": 840})
    framework.write_json(root / "preregistration.json", {
        "phase": "A/B", "seeds": [703, 704],
        "matrix": [{"case": r["id"], "arms": ["baseline", "revision_flat" if r["id"].startswith("revise")
                    or r["id"] in {"history", "accumulate"} else "full_read"]} for r in cases],
        "gate": "Target correctness first; database revision and preserved metadata separately checked. No new semantic regression.",
        "limitations": "Two seeds, fixed sources; full-read candidate applies only to default HTML reads fitting the whole work-view budget.",
    })


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("action", choices=("prepare", "freeze", "run", "worker"))
    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--directory", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--base-url")
    parser.add_argument("--case")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int)
    parser.add_argument("--arm")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    root = args.root.resolve()
    if args.action == "prepare":
        prepare(root)
    elif args.action == "freeze":
        shared.freeze(root)
        hashes = framework.read_json(root / "frozen-inputs.json")
        for folder in ("revision-knowledge", "conflict-knowledge", "baseline-code"):
            for path in (root / folder).rglob("*"):
                if path.is_file():
                    hashes[path.relative_to(root).as_posix()] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        framework.write_json(root / "frozen-inputs.json", hashes)
        branch.verify(root)
        print("FROZEN", root, flush=True)
    elif args.action == "worker":
        worker(root, args.directory, args.base_url, args.case, args.seed, args.arm)
    else:
        spec = framework.read_json(root / "preregistration.json")
        rows = framework.read_json(root / "matrix.json") if (root / "matrix.json").exists() else []
        with patch.object(shared, "__spec__", SimpleNamespace(name=__spec__.name)):
            for index, item in enumerate(spec["matrix"]):
                if args.case and args.case != item["case"]:
                    continue
                for seed in spec["seeds"]:
                    if args.seed is not None and seed != args.seed:
                        continue
                    arms = item["arms"]
                    shift = (seed + index) % len(arms)
                    for arm in arms[shift:] + arms[:shift]:
                        if args.arm and arm != args.arm:
                            continue
                        if any((r["case"], r["seed"], r["arm"]) == (item["case"], seed, arm) for r in rows):
                            continue
                        print("START", item["case"], seed, arm, flush=True)
                        row = shared.run_one(root, item["case"], seed, arm)
                        rows.append(row)
                        framework.write_json(root / "matrix.json", rows)
                        print("END", item["case"], seed, arm, row.get("result"), flush=True)
                        framework.backend_ready()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

warm-knowledge.content:
### SQLite 只读打开 WAL 数据库的分析

**1. 支持的版本**
SQLite 从 **3.22.0 (2018-01-22)** 版本开始支持在只读媒体或缺乏写权限的情况下读取 WAL 模式数据库 [e1]。

**2. 替代条件**
在较新版本的 SQLite 中，即使数据库处于只读媒体或缺乏写权限，只要满足以下条件之一，仍可以读取 WAL 模式数据库 [e1]：
*   `-shm` 和 `-wal` 文件已经存在且可读。
*   包含数据库的目录具有写权限，以便可以创建 `-shm` 和 `-wal` 文件。
*   数据库连接是使用 `immutable` 查询参数打开的。

**最佳实践提示：**
虽然可以打开只读的 WAL 模式数据库，但将数据库转换为 `PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE` 后再烧录到只读媒体上是一个良好的实践 [e1]。

## 引用来源
[e1] SQLite WAL read-only databases (frozen official excerpt) — https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html (source 5fa34fc8ef85871a, 0:915)

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 5. Read-Only Databases

Older versions of SQLite could not read a WAL-mode database that was
read-only. In other words, write access was required in order to read a
WAL-mode database. This constraint was relaxed beginning with
SQLite version 3.22.0 (2018-01-22).

On newer versions of SQLite,
a WAL-mode database on read-only media, or a WAL-mode database that lacks
write permission, can still be read as long as one or more of the following
conditions are met:

The -shm and -wal files already exist and are readable.

There is write permission on the directory containing the database so
that the -shm and -wal files can be created.

The database connection is opened using the
immutable query parameter.

Even though it is possible to open a read-only WAL-mode database,
it is good practice to convert the database to PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE prior to burning an
SQLite database image onto read-only media.

args.markdown:
### SQLite WAL 模式研究报告

基于提供的官方材料，对 WAL（Write-Ahead Logging）模式的各项研究如下：

#### 1. WAL 的读写并发和单写者限制是否矛盾？
**结论：不矛盾。**
*   **读写并发机制：** WAL 允许读者和写入者同时运行。这是因为写入操作只是将新内容追加到 WAL 文件的末尾，而不会干扰正在从原始数据库或 WAL 中读取内容的读者 [e5]。每个读者都有自己的“结束标记”（end mark），确保了单次读取事务只能看到数据库在某一特定时间点的状态 [e5]。
*   **单写者限制：** 虽然读者和写入者可以并发，但由于所有写入操作都指向同一个 WAL 文件，因此在同一时刻只能有一个写入者 [e5]。

#### 2. WAL 引入版本、只读打开支持版本及完整替代条件是什么？
*   **引入版本：** WAL 选项始于版本 3.7.0 [e2]。
*   **只读打开支持版本：** 从版本 3.22.0 开始，支持在 -shm 和 -wal 文件已存在、或有目录写权限、或使用 `immutable` 参数时打开只读的 WAL 数据库 [e2, e12]。
*   **完整替代条件：** 
    *   **保留或关系：** WAL 并非完全替代回滚日志（rollback journal），而是另一种可选的实现方式。
    *   **替代条件：** 
        *   **网络文件系统：** WAL 不支持网络文件系统，因为 WAL 需要所有进程共享一小部分内存（wal-index），而不同主机无法共享内存 [e2, e5]。
        *   **页面大小（page_size）：** 进入 WAL 模式后，无法通过 `VACUUM` 或备份 API 更改 `page_size`。必须处于回滚日志模式才能更改页面大小 [e2]。
        *   **多数据库原子性：** 涉及多个 `ATTACH` 数据库的事务在单个数据库内是原子的，但跨所有数据库不是原子性的 [e2]。

#### 3. Checkpoint 与读者并行时何时停止、为什么、进度保存在哪里、以后如何继续？
*   **何时停止：** 当 checkpoint 运行到 WAL 文件中超过任何当前读者“结束标记”的页面时， checkpoint 必须停止 [e5]。
*   **为什么：** 因为 checkpoint 如果继续运行，可能会覆盖读者当前正在使用的数据库文件中的部分内容 [e5]。
*   **进度保存在哪里：** checkpoint 会在 `wal-index` 中记录它到达的位置 [e5]。
*   **以后如何继续：** 在下一次调用 checkpoint 时，它会从上次记录的位置继续将内容从 WAL 转移到原始数据库文件中 [e5]。

#### 4. Writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件是什么？这些条件是否也是 checkpoint 转移数据的必要条件？
*   **Writer 回绕复用条件：** 当且仅当以下条件同时满足时，writer 会将 WAL 回绕到开头并从起始位置开始写入新事务：
    1.  整个 WAL 已被转移到数据库中并同步（synced）。
    2.  没有任何读者正在使用 WAL [e5]。
*   **与 Checkpoint 转移数据的关系（区分）：**
    *   **不是必要条件：** Checkpoint 转移数据并不要求“没有任何读者正在使用 WAL”。Checkpoint 可以与读者并行运行，只要它不跨越任何读者的“结束标记”即可 [e5]。
    *   **区别：** Checkpoint 是为了将 WAL 内容“持久化”到主数据库中；而 writer 的回绕是基于“所有内容已入库且无读者干扰”这一状态，为了防止 WAL 文件无限增长 [e5]。

#### 5. 这些材料能否证明本机 WAL 比回滚日志更快，或证明整份官方页面从未做过本机测量？
*   **关于“更快”的证明：** 材料**不能**直接证明“本机 WAL 比回滚日志更快”。
    *   **证据边界：** 材料仅描述了 WAL 在“大多数场景下显著更快”（significantly faster in most scenarios）[e2]，并解释了原因（如顺序 I/O、更少的 `fsync()` 调用、写入操作只需写一次 [e3, e6]）。它提供的是**定性描述**而非**定量测量**。
*   **关于“从未做过本机测量”的证明：** 材料也**不能**证明从未做过本机测量。
    *   **证据边界：** 官方页面主要侧重于机制解释和性能特征描述。虽然它提到了在工作站上的测试应用表现良好 [e6]，但并未明确排除在编写文档过程中进行过具体的本机基准测试。

### SQLite WAL 模式研究报告

基于提供的官方材料，对 WAL（Write-Ahead Logging）模式的各项研究如下：

#### 1. WAL 的读写并发和单写者限制是否矛盾？
**结论：不矛盾。**
*   **读写并发机制：** WAL 允许读者和写入者同时运行。这是因为写入操作只是将新内容追加到 WAL 文件的末尾，而不会干扰正在从原始数据库或 WAL 中读取内容的读者 [e5]。每个读者都有自己的“结束标记”（end mark），确保了单次读取事务只能看到数据库在某一特定时间点的状态 [e5]。
*   **单写者限制：** 虽然读者和写入者可以并发，但由于所有写入操作都指向同一个 WAL 文件，因此在同一时刻只能有一个写入者 [e5]。

#### 2. WAL 引入版本、只读打开支持版本及完整替代条件是什么？
*   **引入版本：** WAL 选项始于版本 3.7.0 [e2]。
*   **只读打开支持版本：** 从版本 3.22.0 开始，支持在 -shm 和 -wal 文件已存在、或有目录写权限、或使用 `immutable` 参数时打开只读的 WAL 数据库 [e2, e12]。
*   **完整替代条件：** 
    *   **保留或关系：** WAL 并非完全替代回滚日志（rollback journal），而是另一种可选的实现方式。
    *   **替代条件：** 
        *   **网络文件系统：** WAL 不支持网络文件系统，因为 WAL 需要所有进程共享一小部分内存（wal-index），而不同主机无法共享内存 [e2, e5]。
        *   **页面大小（page_size）：** 进入 WAL 模式后，无法通过 `VACUUM` 或备份 API 更改 `page_size`。必须处于回滚日志模式才能更改页面大小 [e2]。
        *   **多数据库原子性：** 涉及多个 `ATTACH` 数据库的事务在单个数据库内是原子的，但跨所有数据库不是原子性的 [e2]。

#### 3. Checkpoint 与读者并行时何时停止、为什么、进度保存在哪里、以后如何继续？
*   **何时停止：** 当 checkpoint 运行到 WAL 文件中超过任何当前读者“结束标记”的页面时， checkpoint 必须停止 [e5]。
*   **为什么：** 因为 checkpoint 如果继续运行，可能会覆盖读者当前正在使用的数据库文件中的部分内容 [e5]。
*   **进度保存在哪里：** checkpoint 会在 `wal-index` 中记录它到达的位置 [e5]。
*   **以后如何继续：** 在下一次调用 checkpoint 时，它会从上次记录的位置继续将内容从 WAL 转移到原始数据库文件中 [e5]。

#### 4. Writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件是什么？这些条件是否也是 checkpoint 转移数据的必要条件？
*   **Writer 回绕复用条件：** 当且仅当以下条件同时满足时，writer 会将 WAL 回绕到开头并从起始位置开始写入新事务：
    1.  整个 WAL 已被转移到数据库中并同步（synced）。
    2.  没有任何读者正在使用 WAL [e5]。
*   **与 Checkpoint 转移数据的关系（区分）：**
    *   **不是必要条件：** Checkpoint 转移数据并不要求“没有任何读者正在使用 WAL”。Checkpoint 可以与读者并行运行，只要它不跨越任何读者的“结束标记”即可 [e5]。
    *   **区别：** Checkpoint 是为了将 WAL 内容“持久化”到主数据库中；而 writer 的回绕是基于“所有内容已入库且无读者干扰”这一状态，为了防止 WAL 文件无限增长 [e5]。

#### 5. 这些材料能否证明本机 WAL 比回滚日志更快，或证明整份官方页面从未做过本机测量？
*   **关于“更快”的证明：** 材料**不能**直接证明“本机 WAL 比回滚日志更快”。
    *   **证据边界：** 材料仅描述了 WAL 在“大多数场景下显著更快”（significantly faster in most scenarios）[e2]，并解释了原因（如顺序 I/O、更少的 `fsync()` 调用、写入操作只需写一次 [e3, e6]）。它提供的是**定性描述**而非**定量测量**。
*   **关于“从未做过本机测量”的证明：** 材料也**不能**证明从未做过本机测量。
    *   **证据边界：** 官方页面主要侧重于机制解释和性能特征描述。虽然它提到了在工作站上的测试应用表现良好 [e6]，但并未明确排除在编写文档过程中进行过具体的本机基准测试。

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2.2. Concurrency

When a read operation begins on a WAL-mode database, it first
remembers the location of the last valid commit record in the WAL.
Call this point the "end mark". Because the WAL can be growing and
adding new commit records while various readers connect to the database,
each reader can potentially have its own end mark. But for any
particular reader, the end mark is unchanged for the duration of the
transaction, thus ensuring that a single read transaction only sees
the database content as it existed at a single point in time.

When a reader needs a page of content, it first checks the WAL to
see if that page appears there, and if so it pulls in the last copy
of the page that occurs in the WAL prior to the reader's end mark.
If no copy of the page exists in the WAL prior to the reader's end mark,
then the page is read from the original database file. Readers can
exist in separate processes, so to avoid forcing every reader to scan
the entire WAL looking for pages (the WAL file can grow to
multiple megabytes, depending on how often checkpoints are run), a
data structure called the "wal-index" is maintained in shared memory
which helps readers locate pages in the WAL quickly and with a minimum
of I/O. The wal-index greatly improves the performance of readers,
but the use of shared memory means that all readers must exist on the
same machine. This is why the write-ahead log implementation will not
work on a network filesystem.

Writers merely append new content to the end of the WAL file.
Because writers do nothing that would interfere with the actions of
readers, writers and readers can run at the same time. However,
since there is only one WAL file, there can only be one writer at
a time.

A checkpoint operation takes content from the WAL file
and transfers it back into the original database file.
A checkpoint can run concurrently with readers, however the checkpoint
must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark
of any current reader. The checkpoint has to stop at that point because
otherwise it might overwrite part of the database file that the reader
is actively using. The checkpoint remembers (in the wal-index) how far
it got and will resume transferring content from the WAL to the database
from where it left off on the next invocation.

Thus a long-running read transaction can prevent a checkpointer from
making progress. But presumably every read transaction will eventually
end and the checkpointer will be able to continue.

Whenever a write operation occurs, the writer checks how much progress
the checkpointer has made, and if the entire WAL has been transferred into
the database and synced and if no readers are making use of the WAL, then
the writer will rewind the WAL back to the beginning and start putting new
transactions at the beginning of the WAL. This mechanism prevents a WAL
file from growing without bound.
evidence_bindings.label: e5

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 1. Overview

The default method by which SQLite implementsatomic commit and rollback is a rollback journal.
Beginning with version 3.7.0 (2010-07-21), a new "Write-Ahead Log" option
(hereafter referred to as "WAL") is available.

There are advantages and disadvantages to using WAL instead of
a rollback journal. Advantages include:

WAL is significantly faster in most scenarios.

WAL provides more concurrency as readers do not block writers and
a writer does not block readers. Reading and writing can proceed
concurrently.

Disk I/O operations tends to be more sequential using WAL.

WAL uses many fewer fsync() operations and is thus less vulnerable to
problems on systems where the fsync() system call is broken.

But there are also disadvantages:

All processes using a database must be on the same host computer;
WAL does not work over a network filesystem. This is because WAL requires
all processes to share a small amount of memory and processes on
separate host machines obviously cannot share memory with each other.

Transactions that involve changes against multiple ATTACHed databases are atomic for each individual database, but are not
atomic across all databases as a set.

It is not possible to change the page_size after entering WAL
mode, either on an empty database or by using VACUUM or by restoring
from a backup using the backup API. You must be in a rollback journal
mode to change the page size.

[deleted text: It is not possible to open read-only WAL databases.
The opening process must have write privileges for "-shm"
wal-index shared memory file associated with the database, if that
file exists, or else write access on the directory containing
the database file if the "-shm" file does not exist.] Beginning with version 3.22.0 (2018-01-22), a read-only
WAL-mode database file can be opened if
the -shm and -wal files
already exist or those files can be created or the
database is immutable.

WAL might be very slightly slower (perhaps 1% or 2% slower)
than the traditional rollback-journal approach
in applications that do mostly reads and seldom write.

There is an additional quasi-persistent "-wal" file and
"-shm" shared memory file associated with each
database, which can make SQLite less appealing for use as an
application file-format.

There is the extra operation of checkpointing which, though automatic
by default, is still something that application developers need to
be mindful of.

[deleted text: WAL works best with smaller transactions. WAL does
not work well for very large transactions. For transactions larger than
about 100 megabytes, traditional rollback journal modes will likely
be faster. For transactions in excess of a gigabyte, WAL mode may
fail with an I/O or disk-full error.
It is recommended that one of the rollback journal modes be used for
transactions larger than a few dozen megabytes.] Beginning with version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15),
WAL mode works as efficiently with
large transactions as does rollback mode.
evidence_bindings.label: e2

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 5. Read-Only Databases

Older versions of SQLite could not read a WAL-mode database that was
read-only. In other words, write access was required in order to read a
WAL-mode database. This constraint was relaxed beginning with
SQLite version 3.22.0 (2018-01-22).

On newer versions of SQLite,
a WAL-mode database on read-only media, or a WAL-mode database that lacks
write permission, can still be read as long as one or more of the following
conditions are met:

The -shm and -wal files already exist and are readable.

There is write permission on the directory containing the database so
that the -shm and -wal files can be created.

The database connection is opened using the
immutable query parameter.

Even though it is possible to open a read-only WAL-mode database,
it is good practice to convert the database to PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE prior to burning an
SQLite database image onto read-only media.
evidence_bindings.label: e12

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2. How WAL Works

The traditional rollback journal works by writing a copy of the
original unchanged database content into a separate rollback journal file
and then writing changes directly into the database file. In the
event of a crash or ROLLBACK, the original content contained in the
rollback journal is played back into the database file to
revert the database file to its original state. The COMMIT occurs
when the rollback journal is deleted.

The WAL approach inverts this. The original content is preserved
in the database file and the changes are appended into a separate
WAL file. A COMMIT occurs when a special record indicating a commit
is appended to the WAL. Thus a COMMIT can happen without ever writing
to the original database, which allows readers to continue operating
from the original unaltered database while changes are simultaneously being
committed into the WAL. Multiple transactions can be appended to the
end of a single WAL file.
evidence_bindings.label: e3

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2.3. Performance Considerations

Write transactions are very fast since they only involve writing
the content once (versus twice for rollback-journal transactions)
and because the writes are all sequential. Further, syncing the
content to the disk is not required, as long as the application is
willing to sacrifice durability following a power loss or hard reboot.
(Writers sync the WAL on every transaction commit ifPRAGMA synchronous is set to FULL but omit this sync ifPRAGMA synchronous is set to NORMAL.)

On the other hand, read performance deteriorates as the WAL file
grows in size since each reader must check the WAL file for the content
and the time needed to check the WAL file is proportional
to the size of the WAL file. The wal-index helps find content
in the WAL file much faster, but performance still falls off with
increasing WAL file size. Hence, to maintain good read performance
it is important to keep the WAL file size down by
running checkpoints at regular intervals.

Checkpointing does require sync operations in order to avoid
the possibility of database corruption following a power loss
or hard reboot. The WAL must be synced to persistent storage
prior to moving content from the WAL into the database and the
database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL.
Checkpoint also requires more seeking.
The checkpointer makes an effort to
do as many sequential page writes to the database as it can (the pages
are transferred from WAL to database in ascending order) but even
then there will typically be many seek operations interspersed among
the page writes. These factors combine to make checkpoints slower than
write transactions.

The default strategy is to allow successive write transactions to
grow the WAL until the WAL becomes about 1000 pages in size, then to
run a checkpoint operation for each subsequent COMMIT until the WAL
is reset to be smaller than 1000 pages. By default, the checkpoint will be
run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT that pushes
the WAL over its size limit. This has the effect of causing most
COMMIT operations to be very fast but an occasional COMMIT (those that trigger
a checkpoint) to be much slower. If that effect is undesirable, then
the application can disable automatic checkpointing and run the
periodic checkpoints in a separate thread, or separate process.
(Links to commands and interfaces to accomplish this areshown below.)

Note that with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint
is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation
(fsync() on unix or FlushFileBuffers() on windows). If an application
therefore runs checkpoint in a separate thread or process, the main
thread or process that is doing database queries and updates will never
block on a sync operation. This helps to prevent "latch-up" in applications
running on a busy disk drive. The downside to
this configuration is that transactions are no longer durable and
might rollback following a power failure or hard reset.

Notice too that there is a tradeoff between average read performance
and average write performance. To maximize the read performance,
one wants to keep the WAL as small as possible and hence run checkpoints
frequently, perhaps as often as every COMMIT. To maximize
write performance, one wants to amortize the cost of each checkpoint
over as many writes as possible, meaning that one wants to run checkpoints
infrequently and let the WAL grow as large as possible before each
checkpoint. The decision of how often to run checkpoints may therefore
vary from one application to another depending on the relative read
and write performance requirements of the application.
The default strategy is to run a checkpoint once the WAL
reaches 1000 pages and this strategy seems to work well in test applications on
workstations, but other strategies might work better on different
platforms or for different workloads.

new_objects.content:
### SQLite WAL 模式研究报告

基于提供的官方材料，对 WAL（Write-Ahead Logging）模式的各项研究如下：

#### 1. WAL 的读写并发和单写者限制是否矛盾？
**结论：不矛盾。**
*   **读写并发机制：** WAL 允许读者和写入者同时运行。这是因为写入操作只是将新内容追加到 WAL 文件的末尾，而不会干扰正在从原始数据库或 WAL 中读取内容的读者 [e5]。每个读者都有自己的“结束标记”（end mark），确保了单次读取事务只能看到数据库在某一特定时间点的状态 [e5]。
*   **单写者限制：** 虽然读者和写入者可以并发，但由于所有写入操作都指向同一个 WAL 文件，因此在同一时刻只能有一个写入者 [e5]。

#### 2. WAL 引入版本、只读打开支持版本及完整替代条件是什么？
*   **引入版本：** WAL 选项始于版本 3.7.0 [e2]。
*   **只读打开支持版本：** 从版本 3.22.0 开始，支持在 -shm 和 -wal 文件已存在、或有目录写权限、或使用 `immutable` 参数时打开只读的 WAL 数据库 [e2, e12]。
*   **完整替代条件：** 
    *   **保留或关系：** WAL 并非完全替代回滚日志（rollback journal），而是另一种可选的实现方式。
    *   **替代条件：** 
        *   **网络文件系统：** WAL 不支持网络文件系统，因为 WAL 需要所有进程共享一小部分内存（wal-index），而不同主机无法共享内存 [e2, e5]。
        *   **页面大小（page_size）：** 进入 WAL 模式后，无法通过 `VACUUM` 或备份 API 更改 `page_size`。必须处于回滚日志模式才能更改页面大小 [e2]。
        *   **多数据库原子性：** 涉及多个 `ATTACH` 数据库的事务在单个数据库内是原子的，但跨所有数据库不是原子性的 [e2]。

#### 3. Checkpoint 与读者并行时何时停止、为什么、进度保存在哪里、以后如何继续？
*   **何时停止：** 当 checkpoint 运行到 WAL 文件中超过任何当前读者“结束标记”的页面时， checkpoint 必须停止 [e5]。
*   **为什么：** 因为 checkpoint 如果继续运行，可能会覆盖读者当前正在使用的数据库文件中的部分内容 [e5]。
*   **进度保存在哪里：** checkpoint 会在 `wal-index` 中记录它到达的位置 [e5]。
*   **以后如何继续：** 在下一次调用 checkpoint 时，它会从上次记录的位置继续将内容从 WAL 转移到原始数据库文件中 [e5]。

#### 4. Writer 回绕复用 WAL 的条件是什么？这些条件是否也是 checkpoint 转移数据的必要条件？
*   **Writer 回绕复用条件：** 当且仅当以下条件同时满足时，writer 会将 WAL 回绕到开头并从起始位置开始写入新事务：
    1.  整个 WAL 已被转移到数据库中并同步（synced）。
    2.  没有任何读者正在使用 WAL [e5]。
*   **与 Checkpoint 转移数据的关系（区分）：**
    *   **不是必要条件：** Checkpoint 转移数据并不要求“没有任何读者正在使用 WAL”。Checkpoint 可以与读者并行运行，只要它不跨越任何读者的“结束标记”即可 [e5]。
    *   **区别：** Checkpoint 是为了将 WAL 内容“持久化”到主数据库中；而 writer 的回绕是基于“所有内容已入库且无读者干扰”这一状态，为了防止 WAL 文件无限增长 [e5]。

#### 5. 这些材料能否证明本机 WAL 比回滚日志更快，或证明整份官方页面从未做过本机测量？
*   **关于“更快”的证明：** 材料**不能**直接证明“本机 WAL 比回滚日志更快”。
    *   **证据边界：** 材料仅描述了 WAL 在“大多数场景下显著更快”（significantly faster in most scenarios）[e2]，并解释了原因（如顺序 I/O、更少的 `fsync()` 调用、写入操作只需写一次 [e3, e6]）。它提供的是**定性描述**而非**定量测量**。
*   **关于“从未做过本机测量”的证明：** 材料也**不能**证明从未做过本机测量。
    *   **证据边界：** 官方页面主要侧重于机制解释和性能特征描述。虽然它提到了在工作站上的测试应用表现良好 [e6]，但并未明确排除在编写文档过程中进行过具体的本机基准测试。

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2.2. Concurrency

When a read operation begins on a WAL-mode database, it first
remembers the location of the last valid commit record in the WAL.
Call this point the "end mark". Because the WAL can be growing and
adding new commit records while various readers connect to the database,
each reader can potentially have its own end mark. But for any
particular reader, the end mark is unchanged for the duration of the
transaction, thus ensuring that a single read transaction only sees
the database content as it existed at a single point in time.

When a reader needs a page of content, it first checks the WAL to
see if that page appears there, and if so it pulls in the last copy
of the page that occurs in the WAL prior to the reader's end mark.
If no copy of the page exists in the WAL prior to the reader's end mark,
then the page is read from the original database file. Readers can
exist in separate processes, so to avoid forcing every reader to scan
the entire WAL looking for pages (the WAL file can grow to
multiple megabytes, depending on how often checkpoints are run), a
data structure called the "wal-index" is maintained in shared memory
which helps readers locate pages in the WAL quickly and with a minimum
of I/O. The wal-index greatly improves the performance of readers,
but the use of shared memory means that all readers must exist on the
same machine. This is why the write-ahead log implementation will not
work on a network filesystem.

Writers merely append new content to the end of the WAL file.
Because writers do nothing that would interfere with the actions of
readers, writers and readers can run at the same time. However,
since there is only one WAL file, there can only be one writer at
a time.

A checkpoint operation takes content from the WAL file
and transfers it back into the original database file.
A checkpoint can run concurrently with readers, however the checkpoint
must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark
of any current reader. The checkpoint has to stop at that point because
otherwise it might overwrite part of the database file that the reader
is actively using. The checkpoint remembers (in the wal-index) how far
it got and will resume transferring content from the WAL to the database
from where it left off on the next invocation.

Thus a long-running read transaction can prevent a checkpointer from
making progress. But presumably every read transaction will eventually
end and the checkpointer will be able to continue.

Whenever a write operation occurs, the writer checks how much progress
the checkpointer has made, and if the entire WAL has been transferred into
the database and synced and if no readers are making use of the WAL, then
the writer will rewind the WAL back to the beginning and start putting new
transactions at the beginning of the WAL. This mechanism prevents a WAL
file from growing without bound.
evidence_bindings.label: e5

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 1. Overview

The default method by which SQLite implementsatomic commit and rollback is a rollback journal.
Beginning with version 3.7.0 (2010-07-21), a new "Write-Ahead Log" option
(hereafter referred to as "WAL") is available.

There are advantages and disadvantages to using WAL instead of
a rollback journal. Advantages include:

WAL is significantly faster in most scenarios.

WAL provides more concurrency as readers do not block writers and
a writer does not block readers. Reading and writing can proceed
concurrently.

Disk I/O operations tends to be more sequential using WAL.

WAL uses many fewer fsync() operations and is thus less vulnerable to
problems on systems where the fsync() system call is broken.

But there are also disadvantages:

All processes using a database must be on the same host computer;
WAL does not work over a network filesystem. This is because WAL requires
all processes to share a small amount of memory and processes on
separate host machines obviously cannot share memory with each other.

Transactions that involve changes against multiple ATTACHed databases are atomic for each individual database, but are not
atomic across all databases as a set.

It is not possible to change the page_size after entering WAL
mode, either on an empty database or by using VACUUM or by restoring
from a backup using the backup API. You must be in a rollback journal
mode to change the page size.

[deleted text: It is not possible to open read-only WAL databases.
The opening process must have write privileges for "-shm"
wal-index shared memory file associated with the database, if that
file exists, or else write access on the directory containing
the database file if the "-shm" file does not exist.] Beginning with version 3.22.0 (2018-01-22), a read-only
WAL-mode database file can be opened if
the -shm and -wal files
already exist or those files can be created or the
database is immutable.

WAL might be very slightly slower (perhaps 1% or 2% slower)
than the traditional rollback-journal approach
in applications that do mostly reads and seldom write.

There is an additional quasi-persistent "-wal" file and
"-shm" shared memory file associated with each
database, which can make SQLite less appealing for use as an
application file-format.

There is the extra operation of checkpointing which, though automatic
by default, is still something that application developers need to
be mindful of.

[deleted text: WAL works best with smaller transactions. WAL does
not work well for very large transactions. For transactions larger than
about 100 megabytes, traditional rollback journal modes will likely
be faster. For transactions in excess of a gigabyte, WAL mode may
fail with an I/O or disk-full error.
It is recommended that one of the rollback journal modes be used for
transactions larger than a few dozen megabytes.] Beginning with version 3.11.0 (2016-02-15),
WAL mode works as efficiently with
large transactions as does rollback mode.
evidence_bindings.label: e2

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 5. Read-Only Databases

Older versions of SQLite could not read a WAL-mode database that was
read-only. In other words, write access was required in order to read a
WAL-mode database. This constraint was relaxed beginning with
SQLite version 3.22.0 (2018-01-22).

On newer versions of SQLite,
a WAL-mode database on read-only media, or a WAL-mode database that lacks
write permission, can still be read as long as one or more of the following
conditions are met:

The -shm and -wal files already exist and are readable.

There is write permission on the directory containing the database so
that the -shm and -wal files can be created.

The database connection is opened using the
immutable query parameter.

Even though it is possible to open a read-only WAL-mode database,
it is good practice to convert the database to PRAGMA journal_mode=DELETE prior to burning an
SQLite database image onto read-only media.
evidence_bindings.label: e12

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2. How WAL Works

The traditional rollback journal works by writing a copy of the
original unchanged database content into a separate rollback journal file
and then writing changes directly into the database file. In the
event of a crash or ROLLBACK, the original content contained in the
rollback journal is played back into the database file to
revert the database file to its original state. The COMMIT occurs
when the rollback journal is deleted.

The WAL approach inverts this. The original content is preserved
in the database file and the changes are appended into a separate
WAL file. A COMMIT occurs when a special record indicating a commit
is appended to the WAL. Thus a COMMIT can happen without ever writing
to the original database, which allows readers to continue operating
from the original unaltered database while changes are simultaneously being
committed into the WAL. Multiple transactions can be appended to the
end of a single WAL file.
evidence_bindings.label: e3

evidence_bindings.excerpt:
## 2.3. Performance Considerations

Write transactions are very fast since they only involve writing
the content once (versus twice for rollback-journal transactions)
and because the writes are all sequential. Further, syncing the
content to the disk is not required, as long as the application is
willing to sacrifice durability following a power loss or hard reboot.
(Writers sync the WAL on every transaction commit ifPRAGMA synchronous is set to FULL but omit this sync ifPRAGMA synchronous is set to NORMAL.)

On the other hand, read performance deteriorates as the WAL file
grows in size since each reader must check the WAL file for the content
and the time needed to check the WAL file is proportional
to the size of the WAL file. The wal-index helps find content
in the WAL file much faster, but performance still falls off with
increasing WAL file size. Hence, to maintain good read performance
it is important to keep the WAL file size down by
running checkpoints at regular intervals.

Checkpointing does require sync operations in order to avoid
the possibility of database corruption following a power loss
or hard reboot. The WAL must be synced to persistent storage
prior to moving content from the WAL into the database and the
database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL.
Checkpoint also requires more seeking.
The checkpointer makes an effort to
do as many sequential page writes to the database as it can (the pages
are transferred from WAL to database in ascending order) but even
then there will typically be many seek operations interspersed among
the page writes. These factors combine to make checkpoints slower than
write transactions.

The default strategy is to allow successive write transactions to
grow the WAL until the WAL becomes about 1000 pages in size, then to
run a checkpoint operation for each subsequent COMMIT until the WAL
is reset to be smaller than 1000 pages. By default, the checkpoint will be
run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT that pushes
the WAL over its size limit. This has the effect of causing most
COMMIT operations to be very fast but an occasional COMMIT (those that trigger
a checkpoint) to be much slower. If that effect is undesirable, then
the application can disable automatic checkpointing and run the
periodic checkpoints in a separate thread, or separate process.
(Links to commands and interfaces to accomplish this areshown below.)

Note that with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint
is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation
(fsync() on unix or FlushFileBuffers() on windows). If an application
therefore runs checkpoint in a separate thread or process, the main
thread or process that is doing database queries and updates will never
block on a sync operation. This helps to prevent "latch-up" in applications
running on a busy disk drive. The downside to
this configuration is that transactions are no longer durable and
might rollback following a power failure or hard reset.

Notice too that there is a tradeoff between average read performance
and average write performance. To maximize the read performance,
one wants to keep the WAL as small as possible and hence run checkpoints
frequently, perhaps as often as every COMMIT. To maximize
write performance, one wants to amortize the cost of each checkpoint
over as many writes as possible, meaning that one wants to run checkpoints
infrequently and let the WAL grow as large as possible before each
checkpoint. The decision of how often to run checkpoints may therefore
vary from one application to another depending on the relative read
and write performance requirements of the application.
The default strategy is to run a checkpoint once the WAL
reaches 1000 pages and this strategy seems to work well in test applications on
workstations, but other strategies might work better on different
platforms or for different workloads.
evidence_bindings.label: e6

same machine. This is why the write-ahead log implementation will not

Writers merely append new content to the end of the WAL file.
Because writers do nothing that would interfere with the actions of
readers, writers and readers can run at the same time. However,
since there is only one WAL file, there can only be one writer at
a time.

A checkpoint operation takes content from the WAL file
and transfers it back into the original database file.
A checkpoint can run concurrently with readers, however the checkpoint
must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark
of any current reader. The checkpoint has to stop at that point because
otherwise it might overwrite part of the database file that the reader
is actively using. The checkpoint remembers (in the wal-index) how far
it got and will resume transferring content from the WAL to the database
from where it left off on the next invocation.

Thus a long-running read transaction can prevent a checkpointer from
making progress. But presumably every read transaction will eventually
end and the checkpointer will be able to continue.

Whenever a write operation occurs, the writer checks how much progress
the checkpointer has made, and if the entire WAL has been transferred into
the database and synced and if no readers are making use of the WAL, then
the writer will rewind the WAL back to the beginning and start putting new
transactions at the beginning of the WAL. This mechanism prevents a WAL
file from growing without bound.
